title: CarsSearch search request
description: Schema for Requests/<request_id>/request.json — the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for a request's progress. It owns both State (where the search is right now) and Status (how far along it is). The pipeline rewrites this file on every run, reconciling it against Config/brands.json; Requests/index.json is a derived mirror of it.

user_fields.description: What the user asked for. Written once at creation; the pipeline never modifies these.

body_type.description: Closed enum, not free text: two identical-looking requests must search identically. Ids match the shape ids in docs/assets/body-types.svg, so the chart is the enum's documentation.

not_older_than.description: Earliest acceptable model year. Goes into the search query itself, not applied as a post-filter.

special_filter.description: Free-text extra criteria (e.g. 'manual gearbox, RWD'). Empty string means no extra criteria. Never interpolated into a shell/argv.

system_fields.description: Owned and rewritten by the pipeline.

status.description: tbd until the first run picks it up; done once every brand in every active group is terminal (done or failed).

search_state.description: STATE — exactly where the search is right now. Stored structured; the '[Group; Brand]' display string is derived in the UI, because resume needs the structure.

results_path.description: Repo-root-relative path to this request's results.json.

favorites_path.description: Repo-root-relative path to this request's favorites.json.

body_type.description: Kept identical to results.schema.json's body_type enum — tools/verify.py asserts the two lists match.

progress.description: The checklist, mirrored from Config/brands.json at every run start. Any brand present in Config but missing here is inserted as 'pending' — that reconciliation is what makes Config authoritative.

brands_failed.description: Counted separately from brands_done, and never blocks completion — attempted counts as complete.

status.description: Flips to done only when every brand in the group is terminal.

completed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; null until the brand reaches a terminal status.

error.description: Present only when status is 'failed' — why it failed, kept visible rather than swallowed.

brand_diagnostics.description: What the search for this brand actually did, recorded on the brand it describes. Optional: a producer that cannot answer these omits the object entirely rather than writing zeros, because a zero here is a measurement ('the parser produced no cards') and an absent object is the lack of one. Exists so that 'the sites had no cars' stays distinguishable from 'the parser broke' from the committed record alone, months later, with no live debugging session — the two look identical in models_found.

models_suggested.description: Candidate model names the search actually used.

models_discovered.description: Distinct model names the sources themselves published for this brand. Zero means no source could answer and a vocabulary had to be recalled rather than looked up.

models_rejected_as_invented.description: Suggested names no source had listed, dropped before they could reach a URL.

search_fetch_failures.description: Equal to searches_attempted means the sites refused us, not that they had no cars.

parse_failures.description: A source's own parser raising. Non-zero means a code bug or markup drift, never an empty market.

cards_parsed.description: Cards parsed off the search pages, before dedup. Zero with zero fetch failures is the signature of a stale selector.

candidates_checked.description: Listing pages fetched and put through the firewall. Bounded per source, so this is smaller than cards_parsed by design.

firewall_drops_by_reason.description: Firewall drop reason -> count. The only place a systematic drop (every price failing the substring check, say) becomes visible.

search_status.description: The derived search_status for this brand as a whole.

requests_made.description: HTTP requests this brand made, against the per-run cap.

by_source.description: The same counters again, split by source adapter name. With more than one source the brand-level totals stop being diagnosable on their own: '6 cards, 0 kept' reads very differently once you can see it was one source returning 403 while another worked normally.
